audit.why: 52.7% over 148 games matches the arc: even levels 1-2, Cassiopeia's from 3 through the first item, Wukong's at two items. The side-lane and snowball framing is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ items spike says 'stacked armor blunts your magic DoT'. It does not — armour reduces physical damage only, and everything Cassiopeia deals is magic.
audit.why: Stone Skin grants 'stacking armor and max health regeneration'. Against a full-AP Cassiopeia that armour is dead stat; what actually makes him hard to kill late is bruiser health and the Cyclone reset, not his passive.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the late spike, the why and the enemy want around health and the reset, and said explicitly that Stone Skin's armour does nothing to your damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names a single Wukong ability — it says 'his E dash', 'his R-spin', 'the clone'. It also under-states Miasma: only Nimbus Strike is treated as groundable when Warrior Trickster is a dash too.
audit.why: Riot text: Nimbus Strike (E, 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7s) 'dashes to a targeted enemy'; Warrior Trickster (W, 22/21/20/19/18s) 'becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone'. Miasma stops Movement abilities, so it takes away both his engage and his escape at once.
audit.corrected: Named Stone Skin, Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster, Nimbus Strike and Cyclone throughout, with cooldowns, and stated the double-grounding.

audit.whatIsWrong: The clone is mentioned once in mid, but the concrete failure — Twin Fang is a targeted cast and will happily fire into the Warrior Trickster clone — is never spelled out in the do-nots.
audit.why: Twin Fang is a single-target ability with a 0.75s cooldown and a refund only on the real poisoned target; spending the chain on the clone is how the trade is lost.
audit.corrected: Made 'Twin Fanging the clone' the named bad trade.

edits.before: With Q, W and E all up, your Twin Fang chains off Q poison and W grounds his E dash — he can neither leap onto you nor dash out of your cloud.
edits.after: With Q, W and E up, Twin Fang chains off Noxious Blast while Miasma grounds Nimbus Strike (E, 10s) and Warrior Trickster both — no way in, no way out.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze answers his R all-in: it only stuns enemies facing you, so face him as he spins in and the stun ends the trade before his knockup combo lands.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze answers Cyclone: it only stuns enemies facing you, so turn toward him as he spins in and the stun ends the trade before the knockup chain lands.

edits.before: His window: stacked armor blunts your magic DoT and a clone-juke R-reset all-in can burst your boots-less squishy build once he out-items you.
edits.after: His window: two items of bruiser health and a Warrior Trickster juke into a Cyclone that resets on a kill, bursting your build before poison ramps.

edits.before: Save W for his E dash — grounding it traps him in your poison cloud, then chain Twin Fang while he can neither engage nor escape
edits.after: Save Miasma for Nimbus Strike (E) and Warrior Trickster (W) — grounding both leaves him in your cloud with no way in and no way out

edits.before: Stack armor and items until your magic poke stops bursting him and his all-in out-durables your squishy build
edits.after: Stack health until your poke stops bursting him — Stone Skin's armour does nothing to your magic, but raw HP does

edits.before: He stacks armor and out-itemizes your boots-less glass build, and a clone-juked R-reset all-in out-durables you once your poke stops bursting him.
edits.after: He out-itemizes your boots-less glass with bruiser health, and a Warrior Trickster juke into a resetting Cyclone finishes you once your poke stops bursting him.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are honest skill checks: you only have Q, its cooldown is long early, and you've no Twin Fang yet to convert the poison into burst, while his point-and-click Q shreds your armor with a free auto-reset for stepping up. Just last-hit at Q range and stack poke. The moment you hit 3 the lane flips — your Q-into-Twin-Fang chain out-DPSes anything his Q can do, and W grounds his E dash so he can neither jump on you nor flee your cloud. Don't burn W on a feint: bait the clone first, then ground the real Wukong.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are honest skill checks: you only have Q, its cooldown is long early, and you have no Twin Fang yet to convert the poison, while Crushing Blow (Q) shreds your armour off a free auto-reset for stepping up. Last-hit at Q range and stack poke. The moment you hit 3 the lane flips — Noxious Blast into Twin Fang out-DPSes anything Crushing Blow does, and Miasma grounds both Nimbus Strike (E) and Warrior Trickster (W), so he can neither jump on you nor flee your cloud. Do not burn W on a feint: bait the clone first, then ground the real Wukong.

edits.before: This is your lane. Ranking Q and E lets you chain near-continuous Twin Fangs — each one off a poisoned target refunds most of its cooldown and mana, so his Q armor-shred and auto-reset simply can't out-trade you, and your passive move speed keeps you outside his auto range. At 6 his R-spin all-in is his only real kill threat, and Petrifying Gaze hard-answers it — but it only stuns enemies facing you, so turn toward him as he engages, don't panic-cast it backward. Respect the clone: his W can break your Twin Fang target lock, so confirm you're hitting the real one before committing.
edits.after: This is your lane. Ranking Q and E lets you chain near-continuous Twin Fang — each one off a poisoned target refunds most of its cooldown and mana, so Crushing Blow's armour shred and auto-reset cannot out-trade you, and Serpentine Grace keeps you outside his auto range. His armour shred is wasted anyway: you deal magic damage. At 6 Cyclone is his only real kill threat, and Petrifying Gaze hard-answers it — but it only stuns enemies facing you, so turn toward him as he spins in, never panic-cast it backward. Respect the clone: Warrior Trickster can eat your Twin Fang target lock, so confirm the real body before committing.

edits.before: Two items in is where he reclaims it. He stacks armor that blunts your magic DoT and becomes a durable item-dependent bruiser, while you stay squishy with no boots and no resistances — a clone-juked, R-reset all-in can delete you before your poison ramps. Your edge is closing the game while your lead is real: shove with your Twin Fang wave-clear, roam on your free move speed, and take plates on his recall timers. If it goes long and even, his armor and reset out-durable your glass, so make this lane matter before he out-itemizes you.
edits.after: Two items in is where he reclaims it. Stone Skin's stacking armour does nothing against your magic, but his item health does, and you stay squishy with no boots and no resistances — a clone-juked Cyclone that resets on a kill can delete you before your poison ramps. Your edge is closing the game while the lead is real: shove with Twin Fang wave-clear, roam on your free move speed, and take plates on his recall timers. If it goes long and even, his health and reset out-durable your glass, so make this lane matter before he out-itemizes you.

edits.before: Miasma is the anti-dash button — ground his engage and the dive kit becomes a farm bot.
edits.after: Miasma is the anti-dash button — ground Nimbus Strike and Trickster and he never reaches you.

edits.before: - Wukong Nimbus Strike: matchup-defining — His only gap-close — he cannot reach you while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Miasma for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Wukong Nimbus Strike: matchup-defining — 10s at rank 1, his gap-close; step up only on its downtime. - Warrior Trickster is 22s and Miasma grounds that one too. - Stone Skin is armour, so it does nothing to your poison.

edits.before: Spamming E without poison until your mana bar dies — and then standing in Nimbus Strike range with Miasma on cooldown.
edits.after: Spamming E without poison until your mana bar dies — or Twin Fanging the Warrior Trickster clone while the real Wukong resets.
